extracted.intended_audience: GCSE English Language students (AQA Paper 1) preparing for the exam
extracted.subtask_description: A set of exam instructions and question prompts for AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1 (Explorations in creative reading and writing), covering Section A reading questions and Section B creative writing, with mark allocations and advice for candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment split: Section A and Section B
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 40 marks for Section A and 40 marks for Section B; the maximum mark for this paper is 80.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates will be assessed on the quality of their reading in Section A and on the quality of their writing in Section B. Manage time accordingly (advised times given elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of reading (Section A)
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be assessed on the quality of your reading in Section A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section A contains questions that test comprehension, analysis of language and structure, and evaluation of the whole text. The paper allocates about 45 minutes for this section (advice). Answers should refer to the source (insert) and support points with references/quotations from the text. Individual question mark allocations: Q1 [4], Q2 [8], Q3 [8], Q4 [20].

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing (Section B)
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be assessed on the quality of your writing in Section B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section B is a creative writing task (Q5). Candidates are advised to plan their answer to Question 5 before writing and to spend about 45 minutes on this section. Write in full sentences, aim for good English and clear presentation, and leave time to check accuracy and presentation. Follow the task (describe a place at sunset OR write a story about a new beginning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5 marking: content and organisation (24 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Question 5, 24 marks are awarded for content and organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assesses the ideas, development, structure and overall organisation of the piece. Candidates are advised to plan their answer, to structure material coherently, and to attend to pacing and narrative/description choices that communicate the chosen focus effectively. The paper explicitly reminds candidates to plan Q5 before writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5 marking: technical accuracy (16 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Question 5, 16 marks are awarded for technical accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assesses sentence-level control: grammar, punctuation, spelling and range of vocabulary/sentence forms. The paper reminds candidates of the need for good English and clear presentation, to write in full sentences, and to check their work. Use black ink/ball-point pen and follow presentation rules (fill boxes, do not write outside the box, do rough work in the book and cross through unwanted work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2 language analysis criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How does the writer use language here to describe Ugwu’s impression of the city?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The question explicitly suggests including the writer’s choice of: words and phrases; language features and techniques; sentence forms. Candidates should identify specific words/phrases, literary and language techniques, and sentence-level choices, and explain the effect of those choices on the reader, supporting points with references/quotations from lines 5–15. [8 marks]

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3 structure analysis criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How has the writer structured the text to interest you as a reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should write about what the writer focuses attention on at the beginning, how and why the writer changes this focus as the source develops, and any other structural features that interest them. Use evidence from the whole source to explain the structural choices and their effects. [8 marks]

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4 evaluation and supported judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do you agree with the student’s view about Ugwu’s feelings from arrival to the end of the extract?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should consider their own impressions of Ugwu’s feelings, evaluate how the writer describes Ugwu’s feelings by the end, and support their response with references to the text. This is an extended evaluative question requiring balanced judgement and textual support. [20 marks]

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1 retrieval / list task
rubrics_metrics.description: List four things about Master from the first part of the source (lines 1–4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A factual retrieval/listing task testing the ability to pick out specific details from a short extract. Provide four distinct points directly supported by the lines indicated. [4 marks]

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of textual reference and quotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers in Section A should be supported with references to the source text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several questions explicitly ask for support with references (e.g., Q4) or imply it (Q2, Q3). Candidates should quote or paraphrase specific words/phrases or structural moments to support analysis and evaluation; lack of textual support will weaken responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exam technique and presentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and presentation requirements for completing the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly in block capitals for front-sheet details; use black ink/ball-point pen; fill in specified boxes; answer in spaces provided and do not write outside boxes or on blank pages; do all rough work in this book and cross through unwanted work; do not use a dictionary. Time-management advice: spend about 15 minutes reading the source and all five questions, plan Q5 before writing, and leave time to check answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must answer all questions on the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The instructions state 'Answer all questions.' Failure to attempt a question forfeits its marks. Follow the sequence and write the question number against answers if using extra lined pages.
